description:
Section F — Logging Output Safety (example-as-template anti-pattern).

The existing JMAP-6r7c.9 finding flags 'examples/session_fetch.rs prints session.state via Display, bypassing the Session Debug redaction.' The same example prints two additional fields via Display that bypass the redaction this crate landed in bd:JMAP-sc1b.99 and bd:JMAP-sc1b.104:

- examples/session_fetch.rs:99 — println!("username:        {}", session.username); bypasses Session.username [REDACTED] PII redaction.
- examples/session_fetch.rs:117-119 — the loop over session.accounts iterates account ids only (good), but does NOT print AccountInfo.name. So account names are OK here.

The state finding is real and already filed as JMAP-6r7c.9. The username finding is the parallel defect for the username PII (email shape under GDPR/CCPA per the Debug impl docstring at request.rs:200-211).

# What goes wrong (privacy / training-by-example)

Two effects:

1) The example, run against a real JMAP server, prints the user's email address (or other identifier) to stdout. If the operator runs the example in CI, in a screenshare, or pipes the output to a log aggregator, that PII lands in operator-accessible storage outside the user-data scope. The session.state print has the same shape (session-cookie-equivalent leak), and JMAP-6r7c.9 already flags it.

2) Example code is the canonical reference for downstream consumers. A consumer writing their own JMAP client copies the pattern from session_fetch.rs and reproduces the same PII bypass in their production code. The whole point of the bd:JMAP-sc1b.99/104 Debug-redaction work was to teach the discipline 'do not print these fields'; the example then turns around and prints them.

# Suggested fix

Replace lines 99-104 with:

```rust
println!("username:        [REDACTED]");
println!("api_url:         {}", session.api_url);
println!("upload_url:      {}", session.upload_url);
println!("download_url:    {}", session.download_url);
println!("event_source:    {}", session.event_source_url);
println!("state:           [opaque]");
```

Or use the Debug impl which is already redaction-correct:

```rust
println!("{session:#?}");
```

Or replace the prints entirely with a 'fetched OK; N capabilities, M accounts' summary, keeping the URL fields if they are useful for the demo (URLs are deployment metadata, not credentials/PII).

# Scope note

This is filed as a separate bead from JMAP-6r7c.9 because the underlying defect is the same shape (Display bypass) but different field (username vs state). Closing JMAP-6r7c.9 alone won't fix this. Either fold both into a single fix bead or treat them as siblings.

# References

- request.rs:212-227 Session manual Debug impl (bd:JMAP-sc1b.99)
- request.rs:278-288 AccountInfo manual Debug impl (bd:JMAP-sc1b.104)
- JMAP-6r7c.9 (parallel session.state bead)
title: examples/session_fetch.rs prints session.username via Display, bypassing AccountInfo/Session PII redaction
